v1: status-v1.json (16 rounds, weighted 5.12 to 6.05 on the 0 to 10 scale)

R10.summary: I wrote the R10 spec and its annotated image and committed both by name on akinza/construction-loop (54b80062, plain message, no trailer). I traced the three tails in the accepted back study (r03) from an edge map in the loop fit frame. I then fitted Catmull-Rom tail controls to them, in the builder's own [x, y, z, inPlaneRadius, depthRadius] format, and converted them to world units through the back camera. The fit reaches IoU .93 to .98 per tail, and the combined tail footprint against r03 goes from .78 to .93. Depth comes from the first sheet's profile tips, and sweepFlatten is .9 so the tails are round, not plates. The measurements locate the failure at the root. Beyond x -.11, tails 1 and 2 already match r03 within about .01. The baseline roots sit together at one high point (world z -.03 to -.085), so each tail's top edge falls away from the root and the three splay like fingers. In r03 the roots are stacked down one column at x 0 to .03, y .52 to .67 (across the midline), which gives the crescent arch. The spec therefore sets stacked roots, a hidden shingle band under each upper tail with the upper tail in front, background gaps that open only past x -.13 and -.14, a longer tail 3 lying on the buttock, and an even taper with no kink at the tip. It also shows that the baseline's shingle order is reversed: the lower tails sit in front. The spec includes an edge table at ten columns (r03, baseline and target) and the acceptance values. It flags three points for the orchestrator. First, R10.1 and R10.2 cannot pass on the tails alone: even exact r03 tails give trunk .700 and legs .709, and these controls predict about .68 and .70, because the rest of the gap is the arms, torso and legs. Second, in r03 every tail tip points out and down (47, 75 and 79 degrees below horizontal), so R10.4's 'tip curls up and out' should be reworded. Third, r03's back-view widths also peak at 40 to 50 percent of length, so 'full near the root' has to be measured as round cross-sections plus stacked roots with no gaps.

issues.summary: Back of head is a bowl, no head dome inside the fan
issues.evidence: m02 back, m04 head-back: one smooth basin tip to tip with a disc at the neck; back width at .18 is 1.45x the sheet (.225 against .155).
issues.fix: Model a distinct rounded skull dome centred in the fan, about .15 of figure height wide at .18, and pull the fan wings forward and up off it so the centre narrows from .225 to about .16; remove the disc at the bowl base.

issues.summary: Head too deep in profile at chin level
issues.evidence: Side head depth at .22 is .122 against .083 (1.46x).
issues.fix: Cut the lower back of the head and jaw volume between .20 and .23 back by about .035 so the head base narrows into the neck as in m01 left.

issues.summary: Crown does not rise above the fan rim
issues.evidence: m04 head-front: a low lumpy cap level with the inner rim.
issues.fix: Raise a smooth round crown about .015 to .02 above the inner fan rim between the ear roots and clear the lumps on top of it.

history.approach: Melt the rear shingle disc into a rounded skull and occiput with a field-space blur and smooth-union ellipsoids, then tilt the fan and sink the roof beside the crown with a stem-safe smooth vertex warp.

reusable.what: Smooth-unions an ellipsoid into the head field to give a rounded crown or occiput. Keep the ellipsoid distance unclamped: clamping it to the field band shifts the whole box and leaves box-edge creases.

reusable.option: shape_head_silhouette_field.py: top_smooth and rear_smooth (half_width, y, z, per-axis fade, sigma, passes, quintic)
reusable.what: A windowed Gaussian morph with a C2 ramp over the crown or rear centre that melts relief into one surface. The fade must be at least about 10 times the relief change or the window edge shows as a crease.

reusable.option: shape_head_silhouette_field.py: warp{} (tilt_left, tilt_left_low, front_pull, rear_low_pull, wing_recess, forehead_pull, inner_rim_lower, inner_rim_lower_left, nape_pull_gentle)
reusable.what: Smooth vertex displacements applied after meshing, with no resampling and weighted to zero near the face. Keep each slope under 1 (amplitude times 1.875 divided by ramp width) or a shelf appears. The old nape_pull squashes the neck stem; use nape_pull_gentle.

reusable.option: Silhouette predictor (outside the repo: splat head vertices into the fit frame)
reusable.what: It predicts front, left and back head-band IoU within about .005 from a vertex array, so warp parameters can be tuned without a Blender build. It is worth adding to loop_tools if more rounds need it.

issues.summary: Disc eyes stand proud of the face
issues.evidence: m05 nose-profile, m02 left: the eye surface is the forward-most surface at eye level.
issues.fix: Recess each eye globe about .006 to .01 of figure height into a shallow socket and push the brow ridge and upper cheek forward so both stand ahead of the eye surface in profile.

issues.summary: Uniform raised ring instead of a lid line
issues.evidence: m05 eyes-front: the ring has the same weight top and bottom and is a raised rim in profile.
issues.fix: Make the upper lid line about twice the lower, taper it out at the corners, and set it flush instead of as a raised rim.

issues.summary: Knob under the mouth and muzzle reaching the nose line
issues.evidence: m05 nose-front and nose-below: central chin knob; nose-profile: lip mass out at the nose tip line.
issues.fix: Smooth the chin knob into one soft muzzle mass and pull the upper lip back by about .004 so the nose tip leads; seat the nose pad into the muzzle instead of a bead on top.

issues.summary: No pointed locks; the fan is a crinkled leaf with thorns
issues.fix: Replace the crinkled rim and thorn rows with 8 to 10 large shaggy pointed locks per side radiating from each ear root, each about .04 to .07 of figure height long.

issues.summary: No pale inner tuft in the ear cup; rim ragged
issues.evidence: m04 head-front against m01 and r04.
issues.fix: Add a fluffy pointed inner tuft covering at least half of each cup and rising to a pointed tip, and clean the cup rim into one smooth edge.

issues.summary: Fan has no V tilt and blunt tips
issues.evidence: m02 front: top edge level, rolled lumpy tips; 9.7 percent of the reference fan area is uncovered.
issues.fix: Lift the outer tips about .02 to .03 above the crown and taper each to an up-flared point; extend the fan edge where m11 front shows orange.

issues.summary: Fan back is a smooth basin
issues.evidence: m04 head-back, m05 head-rear-oblique, m03 turn-135.
issues.fix: Cover the back face with down-and-outward locks from a crown tuft, with no smooth patch wider than one lock (about .04), and break the bowl lip into lock tips.

issues.summary: Profile shows slabs, a picket of pins and a seam
issues.fix: Remove the pin row and seam and build the profile as a curved shell of overlapping locks sweeping up and back around a visible cavity.

issues.summary: Top edge reads flat from above
issues.fix: Raise spiky lock tips along the top edge toward each wing tip and dome the centre up over the crown by about .015.

issues.summary: Stem neck with a disc at the head base
issues.fix: Blend the head base into the neck with a soft furred transition: widen the neck top at .22 to .23 by about .015, delete the disc ring and fill the nape notch.

issues.summary: No shoulder cap; the arm leaves from a sloping web
issues.fix: Shorten the trapezius slope and add a rounded deltoid cap at the top corner of the trunk, about .045 wide, with the arm leaving under it.

issues.summary: Band across the base of the neck and upper back
issues.fix: Smooth out the horizontal ledge across the shoulders seen from behind.

issues.summary: Side trunk is a tube: chest not deeper than waist
issues.evidence: Side chest/waist ratio is .709 of the sheet (1.09 against 1.54); side waist at .42 to .46 is 1.35x the sheet (.110 against .082); the chest front at .36 sits .035 behind where the sheet puts it relative to the chin.
issues.fix: Narrow the side waist from about .110 to .085 and push the chest front forward about .02 between .32 and .36 so it stands ahead of the chin as in m01 left.

issues.summary: Belt crease and shelf at the hip line
issues.fix: Remove the horizontal crease across belly and flank and blend the waist into the hips over about .04 of height.

issues.summary: Figure reads tubular rather than lithe
issues.fix: After the waist and chest fixes, add soft rib cage volume in front and a slight back curve so the side outline narrows and fills again at the rump.

issues.summary: Forepaw reads as a bud from the front
issues.evidence: m07 forepaw-front, m02 front: narrower than the wrist, with two claws.
issues.fix: Broaden the forepaw to at least the wrist width, about .035, with a blunt rounded end and four digit lobes, each with a claw visible from the front.

issues.summary: Flat facet on the upper arm
issues.fix: Round the upper arm cross-section and remove the flat outer plane.

issues.summary: Elbow does not read from the front
issues.fix: Add a soft elbow point and a slight forearm swell below it so the joint reads at the arm midpoint.

issues.summary: Ankles about twice the sheet
issues.evidence: Front ankle .069 against .033 (2.06x); shin at .85 is 1.61x; ankle over thigh is 1.94x the sheet ratio.
issues.fix: Slim the ankle from .069 to about .036 and the shin at .85 from .087 to about .058, keeping the thigh full (I06).

issues.summary: Double bulge and low shin lump
issues.fix: Merge the two swells into one calf swell peaking near .74 and remove the low shin lump.

issues.summary: Knee reads as a bump
issues.fix: Flatten the knee into a soft kneecap plane.

issues.summary: Hind paws are four equal beads, not a broad fan
issues.evidence: m09 hindpaw-front; back paw over ankle ratio is .431 of the sheet.
issues.fix: Rebuild the toes as larger lobes in an arch with the middle toes leading by about .006, and widen the paw to about 2 to 3 times the slimmed ankle.

issues.summary: Flat instep and short paw
issues.evidence: Side instep at .93 is .063 against .094; side paw length .135 against .155.
issues.fix: Lengthen the paw by about .02 and dome the instep up to about .09 at .93.

issues.summary: Claws are spikes laid on the toes
issues.fix: Make the claws longer curved hooks that leave the toe tips and curve down.

R10.name: Tails

issues.summary: Lower two tail tips point down and out; tails thinner than r03
issues.evidence: m10 tail-fan-back, m02 back; trunk band IoU .673 and legs band .704 against r03.
issues.fix: Widen each tail body by about 25 percent toward the full crescents of r03 and curl the lower two tips up and out; raise the stack so the trunk band fit reaches .74.

issues.summary: Tails fan apart like blades
issues.fix: Close the gaps between the tails so each overlaps the next by about a third of its width, shingled on one side.

issues.summary: Profile reads as leaf blades
issues.fix: Give each tail a rounded cross-section and a curved crescent spine in profile instead of a flat blade.

R10.parkReason: Nick 2026-09-30: the tails are fine; stop working them and put the effort into the legs, body, arms, face and head

history.approach: Rebuilt the three tails from the R10 spec's stacked-root crescent controls (roots stacked down one column, round sections at sweepFlatten .9) onto body-0195 with a new tails-only field rebuild, leaving paws, claws, limbs and the old tail-root fillet untouched.

reusable.what: Runs only the tail rebuild on an existing body. Paws, claws, limb smoothing and the tail-root fillet are left exactly as the input has them, so a later round can re-tail any finished body without redoing the other regions.

Tail controls from the R10 spec: stacked roots, sweepFlatten .9. -b (chosen) raises and thickens tail 1's root third by about .012 and .005, and -c raises it further with no gain. Pass one with --tail-controls, together with --tail-free-body body-0086/attempt-03/shape.glb.

R11.name: Tail root and pelvis

issues.summary: No single sheath at the root
issues.fix: Build one shared root sheath about .06 long before the tails split.

issues.summary: Creases and a pinch at the root
issues.fix: Blend the root into the sacrum and smooth the creases where the tails part.

issues.summary: Root mass covers only one rear side
issues.fix: Extend the root mass across the spine so it overlaps onto the opposite buttock by about .03.

R11.parkReason: Nick 2026-09-30: the tails are fine; stop working them and put the effort into the legs, body, arms, face and head

R12.name: Whole-form coherence

issues.summary: Fan and body at different levels of development
issues.fix: Either add broad coat masses at cheeks, chest, forearm and calf matching the fan locks, or simplify the fan to the smooth level of the body; one level throughout.

issues.summary: No shared coat idiom
issues.fix: Use the same pointed-lock form on the fan front, fan rear and body tufts.

issues.summary: Stray thorns, discs, facets and creases
issues.fix: Clear the fan thorns, neck disc, upper arm facet, hip crease, shin lump and tail-root creases.

R12.parkReason: 2026-09-30: whole-form coherence follows the part fixes; reopen when the head, face, arms, torso and legs reach 5

decisionsForNick.state: Applied: tips curl up and out per accepted back study 0018; the first sheet droops. Reverting is one controls file.

notes: 2026-09-30: torso widths (neck, shoulders, waist, hips) now come from mesh sections (torso_sections.py). The silhouette method had merged an arm or tail into the torso row, so the cold baseline failed R06.1 falsely (waist 1.279); by sections the waist is 1.008 in both assembled-0205 and assembled-0226. The R06 rise from 5 to 7 in round 1 is that correction, not a change to the model.

2026-09-30: Nick said the effort was going to the wrong place: the tails are fine, while the legs, body, arms, face and head are still very wrong. Tails parked (R10, R11 held at their scores). The checklist scores for R05 to R08 were inflated: the arms-down construction pose made body silhouettes unmeasurable and the criteria were local details that a model can pass while reading wrong. Next: an independent gestalt gap audit, a rig with a pose-matched (hands on hips) tail-free fit, proportion levers, and gestalt criteria added to every region.

2026-09-30: weights raised for the parts Nick named: R06 torso 2 to 2.5, R07 arms 1.5 to 2, R08 legs 2 to 2.5. Rubric revised to 80 criteria (gestalt plus fixed-row measurements); a cold re-score of assembled-0226 follows.
